newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary FX futures mkt trades on devaluing forint.
newsitem.headline: Hungary FX futures mkt trades on devaluing forint.

text.p: Trade on Hungary's currency futures markets was spread across the mark, sterling and Swiss franc as dealers continued to trade on longer term forint devaluation, dealers said.

The Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) financial section posted strong turnover of 9.284 billion forints on Wednesday while the much smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw trade worth 520 million forints.

Dealers believe relatively low interests in foreign currencies, notably in the Swiss franc, represent a good tool with which to speculate on the crawling peg devalution of the forint in longer term deals such as September and December.
From April the devaluation rate will be reduced to 1.1 percent per month from 1.2 percent.
September was the favoured month for most currencies, with the Swiss franc ending up 40 fillers at 132.25 forints, the mark almost unchanged at 113.02 and sterling up 60 fillers to 300.60.
Tuesday's central bank midday fix for the three currencies was 121.86 forints for the Swiss franc, 104.71 for the mark and 280.49 for sterling.
Most turnover on the BSE futures market was made up of a currency basket deal for April made up of 230 million forints worth of marks and 106 million forints' worth of dollars.

A basket deal is one in which the trader sells or purchases marks and dollars in proportion to the basket of currencies against which the forint floats -- 70 percent the mark and 30 percent the dollar.
